events.title: Benjamin Franklin Appointed First Postmaster General
events.description: The Second Continental Congress established the United States Post Office and appointed Benjamin Franklin as its first Postmaster General, tasking him with creating a postal system for the American colonies.
events.significance: This laid the foundation for the U.S. Postal Service, which became a vital communication network binding the new nation together.

events.title: New York Ratifies the U.S. Constitution
events.description: New York became the 11th state to ratify the United States Constitution, following intense debate between Federalists and Anti-Federalists, with a recommendation that a Bill of Rights be added.
events.significance: New York's ratification was crucial given its economic and political importance, and it strengthened momentum for the new federal government and the eventual adoption of the Bill of Rights.

events.title: Birth of George Bernard Shaw
events.description: Irish playwright, critic, and political activist George Bernard Shaw was born in Dublin. He wrote plays such as Pygmalion, Major Barbara, and Saint Joan.
events.significance: Shaw is regarded as one of the greatest dramatists in the English language and won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1925 and an Academy Award for the screenplay of Pygmalion.

events.title: Attack on the Moncada Barracks in Cuba
events.description: Fidel Castro led a group of about 100 rebels in an armed assault on the Moncada Barracks in Santiago de Cuba against the Batista regime. The attack failed and many participants were captured or killed.
events.significance: The attack launched the Cuban Revolution; the date gave its name to the 26th of July Movement, which ultimately overthrew Batista in 1959.

events.title: Egypt Nationalizes the Suez Canal
events.description: President Gamal Abdel Nasser announced the nationalization of the Suez Canal Company, seizing control of the canal from British and French interests.
events.significance: The move triggered the Suez Crisis of 1956, a major Cold War-era confrontation that marked the decline of British and French imperial influence in the Middle East.
